input.recommended_action: Rung 2, with operator approval. The three RF fixes (-1822,-64), (-1797,-66), (-1837,-100) are within the 60 m error. (2) Rung 1: re-cue the gimbal S-GIM to the radar position, not the degraded acoustic position. It has found nothing on three cues to the acoustic fix. The acoustic fix is about 275 m from radar. Radar is (-1502, 252), 65 m. The drone is turning toward the shore at about 10 m/s, so lead the cue to the south-west. (3) Keep tracking all sensors. The earlier south-east course (153) was a turn. The drone is now returning toward the pilot (217). Raise the threat level if it heads for housing or other critical assets. (4) Ask the tower whether any aircraft is using the approach corridor (Z-APPR, N-12). The target is inside Z-APPR. (5) Do not use any defeat option now. A defeat option is not needed because the pilot is reachable and the drone is heading back toward them.

options.reasons: S-RF reports a live control link (S-RF 08:20:40), so ROE-5.1 does not block it. Threat is MEDIUM and PID is met, so rung 3 would be possible with operator and control-room approval (ROE-4.1). It is not needed. Rung 2 has not been tried, and the pilot is on the base beach (ROE-1.5, ROE-6.1). The drone is already heading back toward the pilot. If the link were lost, the drone could fall on the beach (ROE-5.3). The target is inside Z-APPR, and aircraft status is unknown, so ROE-5.2 is not cleared. No vessel in the shipping lane is in range: Z-SHIP is 3748 m away (check_line_of_fire).
Interceptor needs threat level HIGH (ROE-4.1). The threat is MEDIUM. Rung 2 has not been tried (ROE-1.5). Aircraft status in Z-APPR is unconfirmed (ROE-5.4, N-12).

No PVID: S-GIM has found nothing (S-GIM 08:20:40) (ROE-4.7). Laser needs threat level HIGH (ROE-4.1); the threat is MEDIUM. Unidentified drone with no Remote ID, with the pilot on base. Keep them informed and ready for ROE-4.1 approvals if the threat rises (ROE-6.5).
Confirm whether Z-APPR is in use, because the drone is inside it. This decides whether D-JAM, D-INT and D-LAS are open (ROE-5.2, ROE-5.4, ROE-5.9, N-12).

Not needed now. The pilot is on the base beach (ROE-6.1). Notify Harborview if the pilot leaves the base on U.S. land (ROE-6.2). Notify the Coast Guard if the pilot is on the water or Canadian waters are involved (ROE-6.3, ROE-6.4).

input.what_would_change: PVID from S-GIM, for example blade spin seen: that would clear one block on the laser and gun, but the threat level would still block them. Heading toward or over base housing or other critical assets: raise the threat level, and a higher rung would then be possible. The tower reporting Z-APPR in use or a crewed aircraft near: blocks the jammer, interceptor and laser. The tower reporting it clear: leaves the jammer open if rung 2 fails and the control room approves. Security finding bystanders on the beach, or finding the pilot concealed or evasive: changes the plan and could raise the threat level. The drone landing or the link dropping: lower the threat level or switch to the no-link case, where the jammer is barred (ROE-5.1). A Remote ID or an own-flight notice matching it (ROE-2.6): lower the threat level to NONE if it is a match. RF and radar positions drifting more than 200 m apart: confidence drops to LOW (ROE-2.5), and nothing above rung 2 would be allowed (ROE-3.4).

The acoustic sensor is about 327 m off, but it is degraded (H-03), so that gap is explained and track confidence is not LOW (ROE-2.5). The drone is over open water at about 55 m, heading 282 at about 10 m/s, and has turned through about 190 degrees in 60 s (repeated passes). The nearest critical asset, housing, is 1369 m away, and the drone is not heading toward it. S-RF has fixed the pilot on the base beach four times, in plain view. Threat is MEDIUM: no Remote ID and repeated passes raise it, while pilot in view and flight away from critical assets lower it (ROE-3.1, 3.2, 3.3). The drone is in Z-APPR. N-12 says the corridor is used only when the tower reports traffic, and tower status is not in my tools. There is no PVID: the gimbal has found nothing on four cues. Rung 2 (security to the pilot, ROE-6.1) is allowed and is the least force likely to work. The jammer (rung 3) is not barred outright, but it is not needed, and it would need tower clearance under ROE-5.2. The interceptor and laser need HIGH threat (ROE-4.1). The laser and gun also need PVID (ROE-4.7). The gun needs CRITICAL (ROE-5.14).
output.reasons: The recommended action is rung 2. It needs only LOW threat and operator approval (ROE-4.1), and it is the lowest rung likely to work (ROE-1.5, ROE-6.1). The key facts check against the tools. Positions, the pilot fixes, the 229 m drone-to-pilot distance, the 327 m acoustic offset, the four failed gimbal cues, H-03, wind 3.1 m/s and the 1369 m distance to housing are all correct. The cited rules and notices exist and say what the analyst claims. Blocked options are correctly handled. The interceptor and laser fail on threat level (ROE-4.1). The laser and gun fail on PVID (ROE-4.7). The gun also fails on CRITICAL (ROE-5.14), and the Z-APPR and Z-BEACH backstops are rated Never (ROE-5.11, ROE-5.13). The analyst correctly flags the unknown corridor status as a condition for any later defeat option. Notifications are appropriate. The analyst correctly asks security to confirm the beach is empty before approaching, and correctly keeps the police and Coast Guard on standby only.
output.notes:
Minor points that do not change the verdict.
1. D-JAM is labelled "NOT NEEDED". Under ROE-5.2 it cannot be cleared until the tower reports no crewed aircraft within 3 km, and the analyst says so. The jammer is rung 3 and needs operator plus control-room approval (ROE-4.1). The analyst did not state this.
2. S-RF telemetry altitude is erratic: 139, -72, 14 and 101 m, against radar at 55-69 m. This is worth watching as possible false telemetry. Position, heading and speed agree with radar, so it does not affect the track.
3. WAC altitude is also noisy (21, 5, 98, 56 m). Radar altitude is the better value.
4. I do not think a stronger response is justified now. If the drone loiters over the beach or heads for housing, or if a payload is seen, the threat should be raised.

shown.recommended_action: Rung 2, with operator approval. (1) Send base security to the pilot estimate on the base beach, about (-1795, -39), error 60 m, to detain and question the pilot and have the drone landed (ROE-6.1). Security should first confirm the beach is empty of bystanders (Z-BEACH). Security eyes on the drone would give PVID only if the report is current and matches the track (ROE-2.4). (2) Rung 1: re-cue the gimbal S-GIM to the radar/RF position, not the degraded acoustic position. It has found nothing on four cues to the acoustic fix. S-ACO is about 330 m from radar and is degraded (H-03), which explains that gap (ROE-2.5, ROE-7.2). Radar and RF agree within about 65 m, and the wide-area camera is within about 45 m of radar. Lead the cue west-north-west: heading 282 at about 10 m/s, so about (-1890, 210) in 20 s. (3) Keep tracking with all sensors (rung 0). The drone has turned east, south-east, south-west and now west-north-west in 60 s. It is now closing on the shore about 230 m from the pilot. Raise the threat level if it heads for housing or other critical assets, loiters over the beach, or if a payload is seen. (4) Ask the tower whether any aircraft is using the approach corridor (N-12). The drone is in Z-APPR. This also decides whether the jammer, interceptor, or laser could ever be considered. (5) No defeat option now. The pilot is reachable and the threat is MEDIUM, so ROE-1.5 says use the lowest rung that works.

new_information.info: Patrol 2 is on the beach now (08:21:30). About 5 walkers are near (-1800, -60). One holds a drone controller and watches a tablet. The drone is over the water just off the beach and no boats are offshore. This confirms the pilot's location and security is already there, so rung 2 can start at once. It also means bystanders are standing where a jammed drone might land or return. Neither the operator nor the other agents had this.

input.pvid_status: Not applicable. The jammer is requested, not the laser or gun. For reference, S-GIM at 08:21:40 gave a visual ID (conf 0.85, blade spin, no payload) and C-04 (10 s old) places the drone over the water off the beach. The laser and gun are not requested.
input.override_assessment: Operator's reason: the drone has circled off the beach for over a minute and should be brought down before it moves over the base. Reviewer's reasons: rung 2 (security to the pilot) is the least force that works (ROE-1.5), the jammer is not needed, and the pilot is reachable. I side with the reviewer. The drone has stayed over open water. It is 1690 m from the nearest critical asset (Z-HOUSE) and has shown no move toward the base. Circling is a weak indicator. The jammer is permitted at MEDIUM with operator plus control-room approval (ROE-4.1), so the objection is about need and safety, not threat level. The operator's concern is about a future move that has not happened. A move toward the base would justify re-assessment, but it has not occurred.
input.concerns: 1) ROE-5.2: no check has been made for crewed aircraft within 3 km. T-1 is inside Z-APPR, which is backstop Never when aircraft are active (check_line_of_fire D-JAM). N-12 says the corridor is in use only when the tower reports traffic, and the tower has not been asked. The control-room info shows no air-traffic entry, so the jammer cannot be cleared. Ask the tower first. 2) ROE-5.3: a jammed Hobby-A drone may hover, land, return to the pilot, or fly on. A return or drop would put it over the beach with about 5 walkers (C-04) or on the pilot. That is a ground hazard to people, and it is worse than the drone circling over water. 3) ROE-1.5: the pilot is located by S-RF (five to six consistent fixes) and seen by Patrol 2 (C-04), so the lower rung is available. 4) Jammer geometry is otherwise fine. The target is 1934 m away, 3510 m from the shipping lane (Z-SHIP), and over open water (Z-LAKE). S-RF is live (ROE-5.1). All defeat equipment is operational. 5) The control room can stop this but cannot step it up (ROE-4.4). Escalate only if the drone turns toward Z-HOUSE or the base, a payload is seen, or the pilot flees or conceals. Even then, clear the tower check first and pair the jammer with security at the pilot (ROE-5.3). 6) Keep S-GIM on T-1. S-RF altitude is erratic (-67 m) and S-ACO is degraded (H-03), so rely on neither.
input.safer_alternative: Direct Patrol 2, which is already on the beach, to the controller holder. They should have the drone landed and detain and question the pilot (ROE-6.1, rung 2). Clear the other walkers from the pilot's immediate area if it is safe. Ask the tower whether Z-APPR is in use (N-12). Keep tracking with S-GIM, S-RAD and S-RF (rungs 0 and 1). Re-assess the jammer only if the drone turns toward the base, a payload is seen, or the pilot cannot be reached. Then also require the tower to confirm no crewed aircraft within 3 km and keep security with the pilot.

input.own_assessment: T-1 is one Group 1 quadcopter. S-RAD, S-GIM and S-WAC agree within about 40 m. S-RF is about 166 m away, within its 150 m error. There is no Remote ID, and the radar track turns about 60 degrees every 20 s, which is a repeated-pass pattern. That gives two indicators, so the threat is MEDIUM (ROE-3.1, ROE-3.2). The pilot is on the base beach, in the clear, and the drone is 1731 m from Z-HOUSE over open water. Those lower the level (ROE-3.3). Rung 2 (security to the pilot, ROE-6.1) with rungs 0 and 1 is the least force likely to work. D-JAM could be considered later, but the tower must first confirm no crewed aircraft within 3 km (ROE-5.2). D-INT, D-LAS and D-GUN are blocked: they need HIGH, HIGH and CRITICAL (ROE-4.1). D-LAS and D-GUN also have a Z-APPR backstop rated Never, and D-GUN is outside its sector and elevation band. N-12 gives no corridor status, so it is unknown.
